0de611461cb91b2b1cee6dfccf2e8da154d6d858f40490c411a021411a04cb3b

Exact chunk fields and text
{
  "id": "0de611461cb91b2b1cee6dfccf2e8da154d6d858f40490c411a021411a04cb3b",
  "source_id": "rta",
  "heading": "RTA s. 135.1 — Rent increase deemed not void",
  "part": 1,
  "text": "Rent increase deemed not void\n\n135.1 (1) An increase in rent that would otherwise be void under subsection 116 (4) is deemed not to be void if the tenant has paid the increased rent in respect of each rental period for at least 12 consecutive months. 2020, c. 16, Sched. 4, s. 24.\n\nNon-application\n\n(2) Subsection (1) does not apply with respect to an increase in rent if the tenant has, within one year after the date the increase was first charged, made an application in which the validity of the rent increase is in issue. 2020, c. 16, Sched. 4, s. 24.\n\nDeemed compliance with s. 116\n\n(3) For greater certainty, if subsection (1) applies with respect to an increase in rent, section 116 is deemed to have been complied with. 2020, c. 16, Sched. 4, s. 24.\n\nApplication of s. 136\n\n(4) For greater certainty, nothing in this section limits the application of section 136. 2020, c. 16, Sched. 4, s. 24.\n\nTransition\n\n(5) This section applies with respect to an increase in rent even if it was first charged before the day the Protecting Tenants and Strengthening Community Housing Act, 2020 receives Royal Assent, provided the validity of the rent increase was not finally determined by the Board before that day. 2020, c. 16, Sched. 4, s. 24.",
  "word_count": 221
}

c2f54625ea915df85ea272c98e140a40f9d54a1865a73ec405a772d8b9c44ee3

Exact chunk fields and text
{
  "id": "c2f54625ea915df85ea272c98e140a40f9d54a1865a73ec405a772d8b9c44ee3",
  "source_id": "rta",
  "heading": "RTA s. 136 — Rent deemed lawful",
  "part": 1,
  "text": "Rent deemed lawful\n\n136 (1) Rent charged one or more years earlier shall be deemed to be lawful rent unless an application has been made within one year after the date that amount was first charged and the lawfulness of the rent charged is in issue in the application. 2006, c. 17, s. 136 (1).\n\nIncrease deemed lawful\n\n(2) An increase in rent shall be deemed to be lawful unless an application has been made within one year after the date the increase was first charged and the lawfulness of the rent increase is in issue in the application. 2006, c. 17, s. 136 (2).\n\ns. 122 prevails\n\n(3) Nothing in this section shall be interpreted to deprive a tenant of the right to apply for and get relief in an application under section 122 within the time period set out in that section. 2006, c. 17, s. 136 (3).",
  "word_count": 150
}

  "id": "78bdbb08ad03091d61e6fc6348085684e086003d7085608996508d9007fe5fe2",
  "source_id": "rta",
  "heading": "RTA s. 191 — How notice or document given",
  "part": 1,
  "text": "How notice or document given\n\n191 (1) A notice or document is sufficiently given to a person other than the Board,\n\n(a) by handing it to the person;\n\n(b) if the person is a landlord, by handing it to an employee of the landlord exercising authority in respect of the residential complex to which the notice or document relates;\n\n(c) if the person is a tenant, subtenant or occupant, by handing it to an apparently adult person in the rental unit;\n\n(d) by leaving it in the mail box where mail is ordinarily delivered to the person;\n\n(e) if there is no mail box, by leaving it at the place where mail is ordinarily delivered to the person;\n\n(f) by sending it by mail to the last known address where the person resides or carries on business; or\n\n(g) by any other means allowed in the Rules. 2006, c. 17, s. 191 (1).\n\nSame, tenant or former tenant no longer in possession\n\n(1.0.1) Despite subsection (1), a notice or document is sufficiently given to a tenant or former tenant who is no longer in possession of a rental unit,\n\n(a) by handing it to the tenant or former tenant;\n\n(b) by sending it by mail to the address where the tenant or former tenant resides;\n\n(c) by handing it to an apparently adult person where the tenant or former tenant resides; or\n\n(d) by any other means allowed in the Rules. 2020, c. 16, Sched. 4, s. 29.\n\nSame, Part V.1\n\n(1.1) Despite subsection (1), for the purposes of Part V.1, a notice or document is sufficiently given to a person other than the Board,\n\n(a) by handing it to the person;\n\n(b) by handing it to an apparently adult person in the member unit;\n\n(c) by leaving it in the mail box where mail is ordinarily delivered to the person;\n\n(d) if there is no mail box, by sliding it under the door of the member unit or through a mail slot in the door or leaving it at the place where mail is ordinarily delivered to the person;\n\n(e) by sending it by mail to the last known address where the person resides or carries on business;\n\n(f) if the person is a non-profit housing co-operative,\n\n(i) by delivering it personally or sending it by mail to,\n\n(A) the head office of the co-operative as shown on the records of the Ministry of Finance, or\n\n(B) the co-operative’s business office, or\n\n(ii) by handing it to a manager or co-ordinator of the co-operative exercising authority in respect of the residential complex, as defined in Part V.1, to which the notice or document relates; or\n\n(g) by any other means allowed in the Rules. 2013, c. 3, s. 42.\n\nWhen notice deemed valid",
  "word_count": 464
}

  "part": 1,
  "text": "Computation of time\n\nHolidays\n\n89 (1) Time limits that would otherwise expire on a holiday are extended to include the next day that is not a holiday. 2006, c. 21, Sched. F, s. 89 (1).\n\nDays on which offices closed\n\n(2) Time limits for registering or filing documents or for doing anything else that expire on a day when the place for doing so is not open during its regular hours of business are extended to include the next day the place is open during its regular hours of business. 2006, c. 21, Sched. F, s. 89 (2).\n\nNumber of days between events\n\n(3) A reference to a number of days between two events excludes the day on which the first event happens and includes the day on which the second event happens, even if the reference is to “at least” or “not less than” a number of days. 2006, c. 21, Sched. F, s. 89 (3).\n\nSpecified day included\n\n(4) A period of time described as beginning or ending on, at or with a specified day includes that day. 2006, c. 21, Sched. F, s. 89 (4).\n\nSpecified day excluded\n\n(5) A period of time described as beginning before or after a specified day excludes that day. 2006, c. 21, Sched. F, s. 89 (5).\n\nMonths\n\n(6) If a period of time is described as a number of months before or after a specified day, the following rules apply:\n\n1. The number of months is counted from the specified day, excluding the month in which the specified day falls.\n\n2. The period includes the day in the last month counted that has the same calendar number as the specified day or, if that month has no day with that number, its last day.\n\n3. Repealed: 2009, c. 33, Sched. 2, s. 43 (33).\n\n2006, c. 21, Sched. F, s. 89 (6); 2009, c. 33, Sched. 2, s. 43 (33); 2024, c. 2, Sched. 15, s. 16.\n\nLeap years\n\n(7) The anniversary of an event that took place on February 29 falls on February 28, except in a leap year. 2006, c. 21, Sched. F, s. 89 (7).",

}

  "id": "ef2c8278e771d0c5485f4ed65142dbdde28e0ffd29163920c27e96b4c9f30509",
  "source_id": "guideline",
  "heading": "Rules for rent increase",
  "part": 1,
  "text": "Rules for rent increase\n\nIn most cases, the rent for a residential unit can be increased if at least 12 months have passed since the:\n\nlast rent increase, or\n\ndate the tenancy began\n\nThe landlord must give a tenant written notice of a rent increase in the proper form at least 90 days before it takes effect.\n\nThe proper forms for this notice are available from the Landlord and Tenant Board. If your landlord has not provided the proper notice, or you believe that your rent has been raised by an improper amount, you can dispute it at the Landlord and Tenant Board within 12 months after the amount was first charged.",
  "word_count": 112
}

24f67b51a6bb8c7ee92df4526f550c536fb477235a8ae893c19efdc926da52d2

Exact chunk fields and text
{
  "id": "24f67b51a6bb8c7ee92df4526f550c536fb477235a8ae893c19efdc926da52d2",
  "source_id": "guideline",
  "heading": "Rent increase guideline",
  "part": 1,
  "text": "Rent increase guideline\n\nThe rent increase guideline for 2027 is 1.9%.\n\nThe guideline is the maximum a landlord can increase most tenants’ rent during a year without the approval of the Landlord and Tenant Board.\n\nFor most tenants, your rent can’t go up by more than the rent increase guideline for every year.\n\nThe guideline applies to most private residential rental units covered by the Residential Tenancies Act, 2006. This applies to most tenants, such as those living in:\n\nrented houses, apartments, basement apartments and condos\n\ncare homes\n\nmobile homes\n\nland lease communities\n\nThe guideline does not apply to:\n\nnew buildings, additions to existing buildings and most new basement apartments that are occupied for the first time for residential purposes after November 15, 2018\n\nrental units upon turnover of a tenancy (the landlord and new tenant agree on the rent amount)\n\ncommunity housing units\n\nlong-term care homes\n\ncommercial properties\n\nSocial housing is covered by the Residential Tenancies Act, 2006, but has different rules regarding rent control and rent increase notices.",
  "word_count": 170
}

902a3591357284b96f5dd36eb7d9a56910686f7aa6e8b630e656422e0cc65af0

Exact chunk fields and text
{
  "id": "902a3591357284b96f5dd36eb7d9a56910686f7aa6e8b630e656422e0cc65af0",
  "source_id": "guideline",
  "heading": "How we calculate the guideline",
  "part": 1,
  "text": "How we calculate the guideline\n\nIt is calculated using the Ontario Consumer Price Index, a Statistics Canada tool that measures inflation and economic conditions over a year. Data from June to May is used to determine the guideline for the following year.\n\nThe rent increase guideline is capped at 2.5% to prevent significant one-time rent increases to tenants.",
  "word_count": 58
}

b62abe1ca85a1ae7c60dade0d3dacd6fcceb6edf923d26fa51c86be1bd257ff7

Exact chunk fields and text
{
  "id": "b62abe1ca85a1ae7c60dade0d3dacd6fcceb6edf923d26fa51c86be1bd257ff7",
  "source_id": "guideline",
  "heading": "A sample calculation of a rent increase",
  "part": 1,
  "text": "A sample calculation of a rent increase\n\nYour monthly rent is $1,000 when you sign a lease on June 1, 2026.\n\nYour landlord could lawfully increase your rent payment 12 months later, on June 1, 2027.\n\nThe guideline for 2027 is 1.9%. Therefore:\n\nan increase of 1.9% on $1,000 = $19.00\n\n$1,000 + $19.00 = $1,019.00\n\nYour rent following this lawful increase on June 1, 2027 would be $1,019.00 per month.\n\nYour landlord would need to provide you written notice at least 90 days before June 1, 2027, in the proper form available from the Landlord and Tenant Board.",
  "word_count": 99
}

f5c67f2bad6d3ffb8c81ecb8430050b1e1520e541055e34b8fea06961361f109

Exact chunk fields and text
{
  "id": "f5c67f2bad6d3ffb8c81ecb8430050b1e1520e541055e34b8fea06961361f109",
  "source_id": "guideline",
  "heading": "Previous rent increase guidelines",
  "part": 1,
  "text": "Previous rent increase guidelines\n\nThe chart below illustrates yearly rent increases, in Ontario, from 1991 to 2027.\n\nYear | guideline (%)\n\n2027 | 1.9\n\n2026 | 2.1\n\n2025 | 2.5\n\n2024 | 2.5\n\n2023 | 2.5\n\n2022 | 1.2\n\n2021 | 0footnote 1[1]\n\n2020 | 2.2\n\n2019 | 1.8\n\n2018 | 1.8\n\n2017 | 1.5\n\n2016 | 2.0\n\n2015 | 1.6\n\n2014 | 0.8\n\n2013 | 2.5\n\n2012 | 3.1\n\n2011 | 0.7\n\n2010 | 2.1\n\n2009 | 1.8\n\n2008 | 1.4\n\n2007 | 2.6\n\n2006 | 2.1\n\n2005 | 1.5\n\n2004 | 2.9\n\n2003 | 2.9\n\n2002 | 3.9\n\n2001 | 2.9\n\n2000 | 2.6\n\n1999 | 3.0\n\n1998 | 3.0\n\n1997 | 2.8\n\n1996 | 2.8\n\n1995 | 2.9\n\n1994 | 3.2\n\n1993 | 4.9\n\n1992 | 6.0\n\n1991 | 5.4",
  "word_count": 133
}

c46d0af95c657c29d63e6ac979d2308905efd045383c19f1da705cb18fce024d

Exact chunk fields and text
{
  "id": "c46d0af95c657c29d63e6ac979d2308905efd045383c19f1da705cb18fce024d",
  "source_id": "guideline",
  "heading": "Resolving issues about rent control",
  "part": 1,
  "text": "Resolving issues about rent control\n\nAs a tenant or a landlord, you can contact the Landlord and Tenant Board to determine whether a unit is exempt from the rent increase guideline.\n\nTo show that a unit is exempt from rent control, landlords can:\n\ninclude an additional term under section 15 of the lease stating that the unit is exempt from the rent increase guideline, and\n\nkeep records that prove the exemption – in case the tenant asks, or there is a dispute.",
  "word_count": 82
}

c97c40201489f9b11e5d36c78e2873e2a37f92954804d7a56c6c4245dd135f3e

Exact chunk fields and text
{
  "id": "c97c40201489f9b11e5d36c78e2873e2a37f92954804d7a56c6c4245dd135f3e",
  "source_id": "guideline",
  "heading": "New buildings and additions",
  "part": 1,
  "text": "New buildings and additions\n\nIf there is a dispute about new buildings and additions, the landlord must prove that the building or addition was first occupied for residential purposes after November 15, 2018.\n\nLandlords might want to keep records, such as:\n\nbuilding permits, permit applications and plans\n\noccupancy permits\n\nnew home warranty documents\n\ndocuments from the builder",
  "word_count": 57
}

c17ab29d9e630483aef144ca2e92dc9fec042e7014b0ffd4fa113dad05660588

Exact chunk fields and text
{
  "id": "c17ab29d9e630483aef144ca2e92dc9fec042e7014b0ffd4fa113dad05660588",
  "source_id": "guideline",
  "heading": "New units in existing houses",
  "part": 1,
  "text": "New units in existing houses\n\nIf there is a dispute about new units in existing houses, the landlord must prove that the new unit was completed after November 15, 2018.\n\nThe landlord must also prove either:\n\nthe unit was built in a previously unfinished space like a basement or attic\n\nthe owner lived in another part of the house when the new unit was first occupied\n\nLandlords might want to keep records, such as:\n\ndocuments from the builder or invoices from the contractor\n\n“before and after” photographs\n\nbuilding permits, permit applications and plans\n\nUpdated: June 23, 2026\n\nPublished: June 17, 2016",
  "word_count": 101
}

4bf7f7bd7f9fefeb51aca011a810d975bdbaccdb4b2db7690e77c5dde0bc752a

Exact chunk fields and text
{
  "id": "4bf7f7bd7f9fefeb51aca011a810d975bdbaccdb4b2db7690e77c5dde0bc752a",
  "source_id": "ltb_guide",
  "heading": "About the LTB",
  "part": 1,
  "text": "About the LTB\n\nThe Landlord and Tenant Board resolves disputes between tenants and landlords. It is similar to a court.\n\nEither a landlord or a tenant can apply to the LTB. Their disputes can be worked out through mediation or adjudication.\n\nIn mediation, an LTB mediator helps a landlord and tenant reach an agreement they are both satisfied with.\n\nIn adjudication, a hearing is held. After the hearing, an LTB member makes a decision based on the evidence that the landlord and tenant present, and then issues an order. An order is the final, written version of the LTB member's decision.\n\nThe LTB also provides landlords and tenants with information about the rights and responsibilities they have under the Act.",
  "word_count": 120
}

6ebf013239401d00cc45d78657ddfba061ca9251b07c54795e6171d66b1e8b71

Exact chunk fields and text
{
  "id": "6ebf013239401d00cc45d78657ddfba061ca9251b07c54795e6171d66b1e8b71",
  "source_id": "ltb_guide",
  "heading": "Increasing a tenant's rent",
  "part": 1,
  "text": "Increasing a tenant's rent\n\nIn most cases, the rent can be increased if at least 12 months have passed since the tenant first moved in or since the tenant's last rent increase.\n\nA landlord must give at least 90 days' notice in writing of any rent increase. The proper forms for this notice (Form N1, N2 or N3) are available from the LTB.",
  "word_count": 63
}

5aaf30e4b71607c342ad160ebcc35e67c66db58e8b9ed35069419dd15e5e5ec1

Exact chunk fields and text
{
  "id": "5aaf30e4b71607c342ad160ebcc35e67c66db58e8b9ed35069419dd15e5e5ec1",
  "source_id": "ltb_guide",
  "heading": "Seasonal rent increases",
  "part": 1,
  "text": "Seasonal rent increases\n\nIf electricity is included in the cost of rent, the landlord can increase the rent to cover the cost of running a window or portable air conditioner installed on or after July 1, 2026.\n\nThe rent increase cannot be more than the actual cost of the electricity supplied to operate the air conditioner. If the actual cost cannot be determined, the rent increase can be a reasonable estimate of the cost. This should be based on information provided by the tenant about energy efficiency and intended usage of the air conditioner.\n\nThe cost of rent must be decreased by the same amount when the air conditioner is removed or no longer in use. For example, at the end of summer.\n\nThe usual rules under the RTA, which include giving a 90 day written notice on an LTB-approved form, or waiting at least 12 months since the last increase, do not apply to a seasonal increase.",
  "word_count": 158
}

b0e650241164fd4a77ae93377f48b2b049494a5f55616d3b6f9ee8897fb1268b

Exact chunk fields and text
{
  "id": "b0e650241164fd4a77ae93377f48b2b049494a5f55616d3b6f9ee8897fb1268b",
  "source_id": "ltb_guide",
  "heading": "The rent increase guideline",
  "part": 1,
  "text": "The rent increase guideline\n\nFor most rental units, the most a landlord can increase the rent by, without asking the LTB for approval, is the rent increase guideline.\n\nThe rent increase guideline is set each year by the Ontario Government. It is based on the Consumer Price Index.\n\nEach year, the government announces the guideline by August 31 for rent increases that will take effect on or after January 1 of the following year.\n\nA guideline rent increase does not need to be approved by the LTB. However, a landlord must get approval from the LTB before they can charge an increase above the guideline.\n\nIf the rental unit was not occupied for residential purposes on or before November 15, 2018, it may be exempt from the rent increase guideline. The landlord must still give at least 90 days' notice in writing of any rent increase using the proper form but there is no limit on the size of the rent increase.",
  "word_count": 162
}

{

  "source_id": "n1",
  "heading": "N1 instructions — Section B: When to use a different notice",
  "part": 1,
  "text": "SECTION\nB When to use a different notice\n\nMost landlords must use this form (Form N1) when increasing the rent. However, there\nare three exceptions:\n\n• Use Form N2 to increase the tenant’s rent if the rental unit is exempt from the\nrules under the Residential Tenancies Act, 2006 (the RTA) limiting the amount of\nthe rent increase.\n• Use Form N3 (Notice to Increase the Rent and/or Charges for Care Services and\nMeals) if the rental unit is in a care home.\n• Use Form N10 if you and the tenant have agreed to increase the rent above the\nguideline because you:\n have done or will do capital work, or\n have provided or will provide a new or additional service.",
  "word_count": 123
}

2b1ee1673d0822c0043a1ecac510f46fa7825cd4b495c907a6adcceb577c01bf

Exact chunk fields and text
{
  "id": "2b1ee1673d0822c0043a1ecac510f46fa7825cd4b495c907a6adcceb577c01bf",
  "source_id": "n1",
  "heading": "N1 instructions — Section C: How to increase the rent and give this notice",
  "part": 1,
  "text": "SECTION\nC How to increase the rent and give this notice\n\nYou can increase the rent if at least 12 months have passed since the date of the last\nrent increase or since the date the tenant moved into the rental unit. If the previous\ntenant assigned the rental unit to the current tenant within the 12 months before the\nincrease date, you can increase the rent if at least 12 months have passed since the\nprevious tenant’s last rent increase.\n\nYou must give the tenant the Notice of Rent Increase at least 90 days before the date\nyou will increase the tenant’s rent.\n\nThere are many ways that you can give this notice to your tenant. You can:\n hand it directly to the tenant or to an adult in the rental unit,\n leave it in the tenant's mailbox or where mail is ordinarily delivered,\n place it under the door of the rental unit or through a mail slot in the door,\n send it by fax to a fax machine where the tenant carries on business or to a fax\nmachine in their home,\n send it by courier, or\n send it by mail.\n\n_____________________________________________________________________________________________________\nNotice of Rent Increase – Form N1\n\n2\nYou cannot give the tenant this notice by posting it on the door of the tenant’s rental\nunit.",
  "word_count": 226
}

5fb2e693e039de32882794f537021eea739df25bd9c40510253c7d884edcb7d2

Exact chunk fields and text
{
  "id": "5fb2e693e039de32882794f537021eea739df25bd9c40510253c7d884edcb7d2",
  "source_id": "n1",
  "heading": "N1 instructions — Section F: What to do if you have any questions",
  "part": 1,
  "text": "SECTION\nF What to do if you have any questions\n\nYou can visit the LTB website at: tribunalsontario.ca/ltb\n\nYou can call the LTB at 416-645-8080 from within the Toronto calling area, or toll-\nfree at 1-888-332-3234 from outside Toronto, and speak to one of our Customer\nService Officers.\n\nCustomer Service Officers are available Monday to Friday, except holidays, from\n8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. They can provide you with information about the Residential\nTenancies Act and the LTB's processes; they cannot provide you with legal advice.\nYou can also access our automated information menu at the same numbers listed\nabove 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.",
  "word_count": 108
}

a68845e8524b0c5bad6303e8560c462512fe41eb2176366c63abaa608c59edc4

Exact chunk fields and text
{
  "id": "a68845e8524b0c5bad6303e8560c462512fe41eb2176366c63abaa608c59edc4",
  "source_id": "n2",
  "heading": "N2 instructions — Section A: When to use this notice",
  "part": 1,
  "text": "SECTION\nA When to use this notice\n\nYou can give this notice to the tenant to increase the tenant’s rent if the rental unit is\nexempt from the rules limiting rent increases under the Residential Tenancies Act, 2006\n(the RTA). Partially exempt rental units can include non-profit and other social housing\nrental units, including care home units that are exempt from the rules limiting rent\nincreases.",
  "word_count": 66
}

159f1606191fb2ba2371af88f610c3a5ea219bb31502ac68565c23a3707b95d8

Exact chunk fields and text
{
  "id": "159f1606191fb2ba2371af88f610c3a5ea219bb31502ac68565c23a3707b95d8",
  "source_id": "n2",
  "heading": "N2 instructions — Section B: When to use a different notice",
  "part": 1,
  "text": "SECTION\nB When to use a different notice\n\nThere are three other notices that a landlord can use when increasing a tenant’s rent:\n\n• Use Form N1 to increase the rent for any rental unit (other than a care home\nrental unit) that is covered by the rules limiting rent increases under the RTA.\n• Use Form N3 (Notice to Increase the Rent and/or Charges for Care Services and\nMeals) to increase the rent for any care home unit that is covered by the rules\nlimiting rent increases under the Residential Tenancies Act, 2006.\n• Use Form N10 if you and the tenant have agreed to increase the rent above the\nguideline because you:\n have done or will do capital work, or\n have provided or will provide a new or additional service.",
  "word_count": 134
}

7621f3cdfae14d92b5777d44f620edbd19bd2126d494dddfc68261583181ea29

Exact chunk fields and text
{
  "id": "7621f3cdfae14d92b5777d44f620edbd19bd2126d494dddfc68261583181ea29",
  "source_id": "n2",
  "heading": "N2 instructions — Section C: How to increase the rent and give this notice",
  "part": 1,
  "text": "SECTION\nC How to increase the rent and give this notice\n\nThe guideline for rent increases set by the Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing\ndoes not apply to tenants who live in rental units that are partially exempt from the RTA.\nIn these cases, the landlord can raise the rent by any amount.\n\nYou can increase the rent if at least 12 months have passed since the date of the last\nrent increase or since the date the tenant moved into the rental unit. If the previous\ntenant assigned the rental unit to the current tenant within the 12 months before the\nincrease date, you can increase the rent if at least 12 months have passed since the\nprevious tenant’s last rent increase.\n\nYou must give the tenant the Notice of Rent Increase at least 90 days before the date\nyou will increase the tenant’s rent.\n\nThere are many ways that you can give this notice to your tenant. You can:\n hand it directly to the tenant or to an adult in the rental unit,\n leave it in the tenant's mailbox or where mail is ordinarily delivered,\n\n_____________________________________________________________________________________________________\nNotice of Rent Increase Unit Partially Exempt – Form N2\n2\n place it under the door of the rental unit or through a mail slot in the door,\n send it by fax to a fax machine where the tenant carries on business or to a fax\nmachine in their home,\n send it by courier, or\n send it by mail.\n\nYou cannot give the tenant this notice by posting it on the door of the tenant’s rental\nunit.",
  "word_count": 272
}

5d56a826f2f515c6fc1105ceed65d87f8945a592bfd71b28ce7481cb83dd4c4b

Exact chunk fields and text
{
  "id": "5d56a826f2f515c6fc1105ceed65d87f8945a592bfd71b28ce7481cb83dd4c4b",
  "source_id": "n2",
  "heading": "N2 instructions — Section E: What to do if you have any questions",
  "part": 1,
  "text": "SECTION\nE What to do if you have any questions\n\nYou can visit the LTB website at: tribunalsontario.ca/ltb\n\nYou can call the LTB at 416-645-8080 from within the Toronto calling area, or toll-\nfree at 1-888-332-3234 from outside Toronto, and speak to one of our Customer\nService Officers.\n\nCustomer Service Officers are available Monday to Friday, except holidays, from\n8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. They can provide you with information about the Residential\nTenancies Act and the LTB's processes; they cannot provide you with legal advice.\nYou can also access our automated information menu at the same numbers listed\nabove 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.",
  "word_count": 108
}
